step1_figure.circuit_type: Common-source amplifier with gate-drain-connected PMOS load and source degeneration resistance Rs
step1_figure.description: Figure 21.8 shows the common-source amplifier with a diode-connected PMOS load M2, driven through a source resistance Rs = 100k and an AC coupling capacitor, with gate DC bias set from a wide-swing bias circuit (SUB_1) through a large isolation resistor.

low_frequency_gain.description: Small-signal low-frequency AC voltage gain (Av = vout/vs)

equation.explanation: Voltage gain of the CS amplifier with gate-drain connected load, neglecting ro loading (Av = -(1/gm2)/(1/gm1)).
equation.assumptions: 1/gm2 << ro1 || ro2; low-frequency operation where device capacitances are open.

sky130_expected.calculation: With matched transconductances gm1 ≈ gm2 ≈ 150 uA/V, |Av| ≈ 1 (0 dB). Including finite ro, |Av| is slightly less than 1, approximately -0.5 dB to -1.5 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: When M1 and M2 operate at the same bias current (20 uA) and have comparable transconductances, the low-frequency gain is nominally unity.

input_pole_frequency.description: Input pole frequency determined by source resistance and input Miller capacitance

equation.explanation: Input RC pole where C_MI = C_gd1 * (1 + |Av|) = C_gd1 * (1 + gm1/gm2).
equation.assumptions: Source resistance Rs dominates input node impedance; Miller theorem approximation is valid.

sky130_expected.calculation: For Rs = 100 kΩ, with typical Cgs1 ≈ 15-25 fF and Cgd1 ≈ 2-4 fF (|Av| ≈ 1 -> C_MI ≈ 4-8 fF), total Cin ≈ 20-30 fF. fin = 1 / (2*pi*100k*25fF) ≈ 63.6 MHz (textbook example is 58 MHz).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by 100k source resistance and total gate capacitance (Cgs + Miller-multiplied Cgd).

output_pole_frequency.description: Output pole frequency determined by output load resistance (1/gm2) and output capacitance

equation.explanation: Output pole created by diode-connected PMOS output resistance Rout ≈ 1/gm2 and total capacitance at output node (Csg2 + C_MO + Cdb).

sky130_expected.calculation: For gm2 ≈ 150 uA/V (Rout ≈ 6.67 kΩ) and total Cout ≈ 50-80 fF: fout = 1 / (2*pi*6.67k*74fF) ≈ 322 MHz (textbook example is 331 MHz).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Output node resistance is small (1/gm2 ≈ 6.5 kΩ) compared to Rs, placing the output pole at several hundred MHz.

rhp_zero_frequency.description: Right-half-plane zero frequency caused by feedforward through gate-drain capacitance Cgd1

equation.explanation: At high frequency, displacement current through Cgd1 bypasses M1 inversion, creating a transmission zero in the right half plane.
equation.assumptions: Output node dominated by feedforward current through Cgd1 balancing gm1*vgs.

sky130_expected.calculation: For gm1 ≈ 150 uA/V and Cgd1 ≈ 2 fF: fz = 150u / (2*pi*2fF) ≈ 11.9 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Since Cgd1 is very small (few fF), the RHP zero is located well into the gigahertz region.

gain_at_400MHz.description: AC voltage gain magnitude at 400 MHz

equation.explanation: Magnitude response well beyond both input and output poles where attenuation rolls off.
equation.assumptions: Two poles below 400 MHz (58 MHz and 331 MHz) produce roughly -20 dB attenuation at 400 MHz.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Both poles roll off the response such that gain is down by approximately 20 dB from DC.

phase_at_400MHz.description: Small-signal phase shift at 400 MHz relative to input vs

equation.explanation: Calculates phase including 180 deg inverting phase shift plus contributions from both poles and RHP zero.

sky130_expected.calculation: From Example 21.3, Phase at 400 MHz is +50 degrees (equivalent to -310 degrees).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Input pole (-90 deg), output pole (-50 deg), and inverting DC phase (+180 deg) result in net leading phase of approx 50 degrees.

time_delay_400MHz.description: Time-domain lead/delay between input vs and output vout at 400 MHz

equation.explanation: Transient peak time advance corresponding to 50 degrees phase lead at T = 2.5 ns (400 MHz).
equation.assumptions: Small signal sinusoidal excitation at 400 MHz after settling.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Output peak occurs approximately 350 ps before the input peak as shown in Figure 21.10.

dc_bias_current.description: DC drain current through the common-source branch (M1 and M2)

equation.explanation: DC quiescent current established by the bias network Vbias4 applied to M1 gate.
equation.assumptions: M1 and M2 in saturation; matched to 20 uA bias generator branch.

sky130_expected.calculation: The wide-swing bias generator SUB_1 is sized for 20 uA reference current.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard operating point specified in Table 9.1 and Example 21.2 is 20 uA.

dc_output_voltage.description: DC operating voltage at Vout node

equation.explanation: DC output voltage set by diode-connected PMOS M2 drop below VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: For VDD = 1.8 V, |Vthp| ≈ 0.42 V, Vovp ≈ 0.15 V -> VSG2 ≈ 0.57-0.65 V -> Vout,DC ≈ 1.15-1.25 V (in 5V process it was 3.85V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Diode-connected PMOS with source at 1.8V sets Vout at VDD - VSG2.

input_referred_noise.description: Input-referred noise voltage spectral density at mid-band frequency (10 MHz)

equation.explanation: Total input-referred noise power spectral density formed by thermal and flicker noise of M1 and M2.
equation.assumptions: Thermal noise dominated by channel conductance 4kT*gamma*gm.

sky130_expected.calculation: With gm1 ≈ gm2 ≈ 150 uA/V: thermal noise current density sqrt(4kT*gamma*gm) ≈ 1.28 pA/sqrt(Hz). Dividing by gm1 gives ~8.5 nV/sqrt(Hz).
sky130_expected.reasoning: MOSFET channel thermal noise divided by gm1 gives input noise around 8-15 nV/sqrt(Hz).

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench for Baker Fig 21.8 evaluating DC bias, AC response (poles, RHP zero, 400 MHz gain/phase), transient response at 400 MHz, and input noise.
